Hotplug sysfs lock acquisition and release semantics and failure modes.
CPU subsystem root, per-CPU devices, remaining CPU attribute groups and sysfs group creation error handling.
Bit operation macros, word sizes, possible CPU count and cpumask helper semantics.
Boot CPU identification, per-CPU hotplug state layout, sync and online target values and booted-once mask.
Attack vector enumeration values, KVM gating, warning helper and matching and string splitting helpers.

findings.text: SMT control store accepts textual requests for on, off and forceoff plus integer thread counts. It rejects writes while already force-disabled and when the platform reports no support, validates numeric counts, then updates the requested thread count under a hotplug lock and grows or shrinks capacity through separate helpers. A build without the feature exposes only a failing store.

Two sysfs readouts are provided: one for the SMT control state and one for current SMT activity. The control readout shows either a numeric thread count during partial enablement or a symbolic state name, while the activity readout reports scheduler-observed SMT activity. The control write path delegates directly to the shared store routine.

SMT control moves among enabled, disabled, force-disabled and unsupported or unimplemented states. Raising the requested thread count triggers enablement; lowering it triggers disablement. A transition into force-disabled also triggers disablement even without a count change, and once force-disabled the store refuses further changes.
User-visible SMT state names are on for enabled, off for disabled, forceoff for force-disabled, notsupported when unsupported, and notimplemented when unimplemented.
An attribute collection exposes control and active entries under a group named smt. The group references a null-terminated attribute list and is attached beneath the CPU subsystem root.

Early initialization creates the smt group under the CPU bus root, then creates a root CPU group and per-possible-CPU groups for every present CPU device. Any group creation failure aborts initialization with an error and skips remaining devices.

A read-only two-dimensional bit table provides precomputed single-bit masks. Row zero is empty and each later row holds exactly one set bit corresponding to its index, with extra rows present on wider words.

Global CPU membership state comprises possible, online, enabled, present, active and dying masks plus possible and online counts. Possible state is immutable after early boot in one configuration and fully populated in another, while the remaining masks and the online count are optimized for frequent reads.
Public helpers initialize present and possible masks from a supplied mask and mark individual CPUs online or possible. Possible initialization also refreshes the possible count from mask weight.

Online and possible counters change only on actual membership transitions. Setting online uses an atomic test-and-set and increments only on first arrival; clearing uses test-and-clear and decrements only on departure. Possible membership similarly adjusts its count only when the bit flips.

Boot CPU setup marks the current processor as online, active, present and possible, covering both single and multi processor builds, and records its identity as the boot processor when symmetric multiprocessing is present.
Hotplug boot setup records that the boot CPU has booted once and initializes its synchronization and hotplug progression state to online for both current and target values.

Mitigation mode starts in automatic and can move to off or automatic without SMT through a global command line option. Off clears all attack vector flags and disables SMT mitigations; automatic without SMT enables SMT mitigations. Optional comma-separated vector options then clear individual vectors or cross-thread protection.
Accepted command line spellings include auto, auto with nosmt, and off for global mode, plus no_user_kernel, no_user_user, no_guest_host, no_guest_guest and no_cross_thread for selective reduction.

User-kernel and user-user vectors default to mitigated, while guest-host and guest-guest vectors default according to virtualization support. Queries for defined vectors return the stored flag; queries outside the table warn once and report not mitigated. SMT mitigation policy defaults to automatic.

CPU power management exposes registration and unregistration plus paired enter and exit operations for both a single CPU and a cluster. Enter operations use a robust notification pair with a failure companion; exit operations use a single notification.

A dedicated raw spinlock guards the power notifier chain with interrupt state preserved across register, unregister and robust delivery. Plain exit delivery instead runs under read-side RCU protection without holding that lock.

System suspend enters CPU power management before cluster power management and aborts if the first stage fails. Resume performs the reverse order, leaving cluster before CPU. Enter stages pair an enter event with a failed-enter event; exit stages emit single exit events.

Power notification state pairs a raw notifier chain with its lock in one holder. A syscore operations object binds suspend and resume callbacks, wrapped in a syscore record that is registered once during initialization.
Thin wrappers adapt a raw notifier head to generic chain primitives for plain delivery, robust paired delivery, insertion and removal.

Insertion keeps the chain ordered by decreasing priority. Reinserting the same block warns and reports already present, and when uniqueness is requested an equal priority collision reports busy. Publication uses ordered assignment with a registration trace.

Removal scans for block identity, unlinks the first match through ordered assignment with an unregistration trace, and reports success. If no entry matches, it reports absent without modifying the chain.
Control page allocation dispatches on image kind, using the normal path for default images and the crash-reservation path for crash images when crash dumping is present.

The normal allocator repeatedly requests a contiguous block until it finds one outside the control limit and outside every image destination range. Successful blocks join the image control list; accidentally allocated destination blocks are collected separately and released.

The crash allocator advances an aligned hole through the crash reservation, skipping overlaps with image segments and stopping at the reservation end or control limit. On finding a non-overlapping hole it converts the address to pages and advances the next-search cursor past the allocation.
Destination overlap is decided by interval intersection against every segment memory extent. Any shared byte reports overlap; otherwise the range is reported clear.

Fresh control pages record their allocation order, are marked reserved across the whole block, pass through an architecture hook, and are optionally zeroed. Release invokes a pre-free hook, clears reservation on each page, then frees the block. List release unlinks each entry before freeing it.

Vmcoreinfo safecopy setup applies only when crash dumping is enabled and the image is a crash image. It reserves appropriately ordered control pages, maps them for access, stores the mapping in the image, and copies current vmcoreinfo content into the safe area while recording the pointer.
Crash notes are held in per-CPU storage. A separate global safecopy pointer tracks the mapped vmcoreinfo copy and is updated whenever a new mapping is established.
The contiguous allocation DMA wait timeout is ten seconds.
Messages from the crash core module carry that module name as a prefix.
The SMT store holds the device hotplug sysfs lock from validation of the hotplug path through the thread count update and enable or disable call, releasing it before returning the outcome.

Atomic updates to the online count do not make unsynchronized readers safe during concurrent hotplug. Shutdown and crash paths may also invoke the online helper from broadcast contexts rather than normal serialized hotplug.

Malformed or out-of-range SMT requests fail validation without changing state. Force-disabled and unsupported configurations fail with distinct permission and device errors, so callers must distinguish permanent refusal from absent support.

Unsupported global or vector mitigation spellings, missing separators, or use on builds without vector support leave prior settings in place and emit a critical warning that the system may remain vulnerable. A build without mitigations ignores the option entirely.
Duplicate notifier insertion and removal of an unregistered block are reported as errors rather than silently ignored, so callers must handle already-present and absent outcomes.
Page allocation aborts when a fatal signal is pending, and vmcoreinfo reservation or mapping failures warn and report out-of-memory without establishing a safecopy.
